competences: The learner identifies key facts about ways of acquiring leadership — part b.
The learner explains how leaders are selected and the qualities expected of them.
languageCompetence: Pronounce, spell and read election, appointment, inheritance, volunteer, ballot, leader and leadership.
objectives: By the end of the lesson learners should name facts relating to ways of acquiring leadership — part b.
By the end of the lesson learners should answer the sourced exercise questions accurately.
priorKnowledge: Learners have studied civic, political, cultural and voluntary leaders during earlier SST lessons.
materials: P4 SST source notes on leadership
references: Primary 4 Social Studies Notes for Terms 1–3

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher recalls earlier lessons about district leadership and introduces ways of acquiring leadership — part b by asking "4. State any two advantages of choosing leaders using secret ballot system.". They identify pupils' prior knowledge and set the objective.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall previously studied district leaders, answer the opening question and state what they know about choosing leaders.

steps.content: Political leaders can be selected through elections. Civic leaders can receive authority through appointment. Cultural leaders may inherit leadership. Voluntary leaders offer their services willingly. Some elections use a secret ballot system. Some elections use an open voting system. Ballot papers are used during elections. The ballot box keeps ballots after voting. The voters' register lists eligible voters. A polling station is the place where voting happens. Polling officers are in charge of polling stations. Election candidates stand to be voted into office.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher presents the documented points for "Remember", including "Political leaders can be selected through elections. Civic leaders can receive authority through appointment." They check understanding using "5. Give any two disadvantages of the secret ballot electoral system." and explain the correct response.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners identify the leadership roles or election methods, respond to questions, and copy the referenced notes into their books.

steps.content: 4. State any two advantages of choosing leaders using secret ballot system. | 5. Give any two disadvantages of the secret ballot electoral system. | 6. State any three advantages of open elections. | 7. Give any one disadvantage of choosing leaders through open elections. | 12. Give any three ways elections are important in a country.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher sets the original questions "4. State any two advantages of choosing leaders using secret ballot system." and "5. Give any two disadvantages of the secret ballot electoral system." and supervises individual written answers. They mark and correct the responses using the source references.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners write answers independently, compare them with class notes and correct any inaccurate points after marking.

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher reviews the main ideas and checks progress with "6. State any three advantages of open elections." and "7. Give any one disadvantage of choosing leaders through open elections.". They assign the remaining sourced question as homework.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer final oral questions, explain a relevant fact and record the original homework question.

assessment: Assess learners with "4. State any two advantages of choosing leaders using secret ballot system.", "5. Give any two disadvantages of the secret ballot electoral system.", and "6. State any three advantages of open elections.". Mark the answers according to the lesson notes.
homework: Complete the original question "12. Give any three ways elections are important in a country."
